subject: Linguistics
title: Semantic Change
description: Learn Semantic Change in one minute.

hook.text: 'Awful' once meant 'full of awe'—a compliment. Now it means terrible.

buildup.text: Word meanings drift over centuries through broadening, narrowing, and shifts in evaluation.

discovery.text: 'Meat' once meant any food; it narrowed to mean only animal flesh over time.

twist.text: 'Nice' started as 'ignorant' in Latin, drifted through 'foolish,' and ended up meaning 'pleasant.'

climax.text: Semantic change is constant—today's slang is tomorrow's standard vocabulary.

punchline.text: Words change their minds—slowly, but always.
